outcomes.text: Know that computers internally represent all data in binary
Know that data is converted to binary, processed using logic gates
Identify and use the standard symbols for logic gates
Demonstrate the function of each logic gate limited to: (a) NOT (b) AND (c) OR (d) NAND (e) NOR (f) XOR. Note: Logic gates will be limited to a maximum of two inputs
Know how data storage is measured, limited to: (a) bit (b) nibble (c) byte (d) kibibyte (KiB) (e) mebibyte (MiB) (f) gibibyte (GiB) (g) tebibyte (TiB)
Convert between each data storage measurement in 1.1.5
Know the base of the denary, binary and hexadecimal number systems

Convert between: (a) denary and binary (b) denary and hexadecimal (c) hexadecimal and binary. Note: Candidates will be expected to do conversions in both directions, values used will be positive integers only, maximum binary number length of 12 bits
Explain the advantages of using hexadecimal as an understandable representation of binary and identify examples where hexadecimal is used
Add two positive 8-bit binary integers
Describe overflow and how it can create errors in binary addition
Perform logical left and right shifts of multiple places on a positive 8-bit binary integer
Explain the effects of logical left and right shifts
Perform cyclic left and right shifts of multiple places on a positive 8-bit binary integer
Explain the effects of cyclic left and right shifts
Convert positive and negative binary or denary integers to their two’s complement 8-bit representation
Convert two’s complement 8-bit integers back to binary or denary
Know that computers store characters as binary numbers
Understand that a character set is a set of characters that have corresponding numeric codes
Describe how a computer represents text using character sets
Describe the features of the character sets: (a) American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII) (b) Unicode
Describe the advantages and disadvantages of: (a) ASCII (b) Unicode
Describe how a computer represents analogue sound, including: (a) sample rate (b) sample resolution
Explain the effects of changing the sample rate and sample resolution
Know that a bitmap image is made up of pixels
Describe how a computer uses binary to represent a bitmap image, including: (a) resolution (b) colour depth
Explain the effects of changing the resolution or the colour depth on a bitmap image
Explain the purpose of data compression for transmission and storage
Explain the impact of data compression for transmission and storage
Explain how images, sound and video files are compressed using lossy compression methods

Explain how text, images, video and sound files are compressed using the lossless compression methods of run length encoding (RLE) and Huffman coding. Note: Candidates will not be required to create or interpret a Huffman tree
Describe the advantages and disadvantages of lossy and lossless compression methods and identify where each method would be appropriate from a given scenario

Use logic gates to create logic circuits from a: (a) problem statement (b) logic expression (c) truth table. Note: Circuits must be created for the statement given, without simplification. Note: Logic circuits will be limited to a maximum of three inputs and one output
Complete a truth table from a: (a) problem statement (b) logic expression (c) logic circuit
Write a logic expression from a: (a) problem statement (b) logic circuit (c) truth table
Describe the role of the central processing unit (CPU) in a computer
Describe a microprocessor as a type of integrated circuit on a single chip

Describe the purpose of the components in a CPU, limited to the: (a) arithmetic logic unit (ALU) (b) control unit (CU) (c) program counter (PC) (d) memory address register (MAR) (e) memory data register (MDR) (f) current instruction register (CIR) (g) accumulator (ACC) (h) address bus (i) data bus (j) control bus (k) cache (l) cores (m) clock

subtopics.title: Von Neumann and the FDE cycle

outcomes.text: Describe the roles of the central processing unit (CPU) and random access memory (RAM) in the von Neumann architecture
Describe the process of the fetch–decode–execute (FDE) cycle, including the role of each component in the CPU, in a computer that has a von Neumann architecture
Explain how the number of cores, size of the cache and the clock speed can affect the performance of a CPU
Describe the purpose of an instruction set for a CPU
Explain the purpose and the role of primary storage in a computer, limited to: (a) random access memory (RAM) (b) read only memory (ROM) (c) cache (d) registers
Describe the similarities and differences between RAM and ROM
Explain the purpose and the role of secondary storage in a computer
Describe the similarities and differences between primary and secondary storage
Describe the operation of magnetic and solid-state storage, including how data is read from and written to each type of storage
Explain the differences between magnetic, and solid-state storage
Describe how virtual memory is created and used
Explain why virtual memory is necessary
Understand that data is separated into packets to be transmitted
Describe the structure of a data packet, limited to: (a) the packet header (b) the payload (c) the trailer
State what is included in the packet header, the payload and the trailer
Describe the process of packet switching, including: (a) packets can take different routes (b) routers make forwarding decisions (c) at the destination packets are reassembled
Describe how data is transmitted from one device to another using different methods of data transmission, limited to: (a) serial (b) parallel (c) simplex (d) half-duplex (e) full duplex
Identify typical applications for each of the transmission methods in 3.2.1
Explain the suitability, advantages and disadvantages of the transmission methods in 3.2.1
Describe the purpose of a network interface card (NIC)
Describe the format and purpose of a media access control (MAC) address
State that each NIC has a unique identifier (MAC address)
Describe the function of a switch limited to storing the MAC addresses of connected devices
Describe the purpose of an internet protocol (IP) address in uniquely identifying networks and devices on the internet
Describe the format of an IP address

Explain the features of and the differences between IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, including: (a) IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (written as four sets of denary numbers, separated by dots) (b) IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses (written as eight sets of hexadecimal numbers, separated by colons)

Explain the features of and the differences between static and dynamic IP addresses, including: (a) static IP addresses remain fixed and are often used for servers or hosting services (b) dynamic IP addresses are allocated temporarily by an ISP or home router when a device connects to the internet
Describe the functions of a router

topics.title: 3.4 The Internet and the World Wide Web

outcomes.text: Describe the purpose of a uniform resource locator (URL)
Describe the structure of a URL
Describe the purpose and operation of hypertext transfer protocol (HTTP) as the protocol for requesting and delivering web resources
Describe the purpose and operation of hypertext transfer protocol secure (HTTPS) as a secure version of HTTP that uses encryption to ensure secure communication

Describe how web pages are located, retrieved and displayed on a device when a user inputs a URL, including the role of: (a) the web browser (b) IP addresses (c) domain name system (DNS) (d) the webserver (e) hypertext markup language (HTML)
Understand the role of the DNS in translating human-readable domain names into IP addresses so that browsers can locate web servers to make HTTP requests
Understand that cookies are small text files that store pieces of data stored by a web browser
Explain the difference between session cookies and persistent cookies
Describe the features of the cloud and cloud services
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of storing data on the cloud in comparison to storing data locally
Explain the difference between cloud storage models and when they would be used, limited to: (a) public (b) private (c) hybrid
Describe how errors can occur during data storage, data transmission and data entry
Describe how methods detect errors and how errors are corrected, including: (a) parity bit (odd and even) (b) parity block check (odd and even) (c) echo check (d) checksum (e) check digit
Calculate a parity bit or parity byte for a given piece of binary data

Identify examples of when a check digit is used, including: (a) International Standard Book Number (ISBN) (b) bar codes (c) airline tickets (d) bank account numbers. Note: Candidates will not be required to calculate a check digit or checksum
Describe how an automatic repeat reQuest (ARQ) can be used to acknowledge whether data is received without error, including the use of positive and negative acknowledgements
State the core principles of cybersecurity as: (a) confidentiality (b) integrity (c) authenticity (d) availability (e) non-repudiation
Describe how each of the core principles of cybersecurity can be threatened

Describe the aims and processes involved in cybersecurity threats, limited to: (a) brute-force attack (b) data interception (c) distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack (d) hacking and unauthorised access (e) malware (virus, worm, Trojan horse, spyware, adware, ransomware) (f) pharming (g) phishing (h) social engineering (i) structured query language (SQL) injection

Explain how solutions are used to help keep data safe from cybersecurity threats, limited to: (a) access levels (b) anti-malware, including anti-virus and anti-spyware (c) authentication (username and password, biometrics, two-step verification) (d) automating software updates (e) checking the spelling and tone of communications (f) checking the URL attached to a link (g) firewalls (h) privacy settings (i) proxy servers (j) transport layer security (TLS) (k) virtual private network (VPN)
Describe the purpose of encryption when storing or transmitting data, including: (a) protecting confidentiality (b) ensuring integrity (c) supporting authenticity and non-repudiation
Explain how data is encrypted using symmetric and asymmetric encryption methods

Describe the purpose of an operating system as the software layer that manages the system resources that provides a platform for running application software and an interface for users to interact with the computer hardware
Describe how an operating system manages user accounts and system security
Describe how an operating system manages files, including: (a) file systems (b) directories
Describe how an operating system manages memory, including: (a) allocating memory to processes (b) loading processes into RAM (c) paging and segmentation (d) virtual memory (e) memory protection
Describe how an operating system manages processes, including: (a) scheduling processes (b) enabling inter-process communication
Describe how an operating system manages peripherals and device drivers

Describe how an operating system handles interrupts, including: (a) the conditions that cause hardware and software interrupts (b) how an interrupt is handled with an interrupt service routine (ISR) (c) how the operating system ensures the interrupted process can later resume
Describe the features of: (a) high-level languages (b) low-level languages, including assembly language (c) syntax
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of high-level and low-level languages
Describe the features and operation of: (a) a compiler (b) an interpreter (c) an assembler
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of each translator and identify the most appropriate for use in a given scenario

Describe the purpose of an integrated development environment (IDE) as a tool to support software development with various functionality provided, including: (a) code editors (b) run-time environment (c) translators (d) error diagnostics (e) auto-completion / code completion (f) prettyprint (g) AI assistance
Understand that a microcontroller is a complete computer system on a single chip, containing a processor, a small amount of RAM and ROM, and I/O ports
Understand that sensors are used to detect changes in the physical environment and an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is used to convert analogue signals into digital data
Identify a suitable sensor for a given scenario
Describe the purpose and characteristics of an embedded system
Identify systems, devices and machines in which embedded systems are commonly used
Understand that actuators are devices that do actions in response to the output from a microcontroller
Describe how sensors, microcontrollers and actuators can be used in collaboration to create automated systems
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using automated systems for: (a) transport (b) agriculture (c) domestic settings (d) retail
Evaluate the implications automated systems have on: (a) employment (b) safety (c) environmental sustainability
Define robotics as a branch of technology that incorporates the design, construction, operation and use of robots

Describe the characteristics of a robot, including: (a) a mechanical structure or framework (b) electronic components, such as sensors, microcontrollers and networking hardware, motors, actuators and power supplies (c) programmability
Describe the roles that robots can perform in the following areas: (a) industry (b) agriculture (c) medicine
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of the use of robots in the areas listed in 6.2.3
Evaluate the implications of using robots for: (a) employment (b) safety (c) environmental sustainability
Understand that artificial intelligence (AI) is a branch of computer science focused on the simulation of intelligent behaviours by computers

Describe the main features of AI, including: (a) the collection of data (b) the rules for using that data (c) the ability to process large data sets (d) the ability to reason (e) the ability to learn and adapt using supervised learning, unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning

Describe common applications of AI, limited to: (a) recommendation systems (b) natural language processing and large language models (LLMs) (c) generative AI, including, images and video (d) computer vision, including links to robotics and automated systems (e) predictive analytics
Understand the structure of neural networks as the: (a) input layer (b) hidden layer(s) (c) output layer
Explain the purpose of machine learning including how neural networks are used
Identify different ways that AI can be used in a given context
Evaluate the fairness and bias in data and AI systems
Evaluate the ethical and societal considerations of AI
Evaluate the implications of AI for: (a) employment (b) safety (c) environmental sustainability
Describe the differences between a quantum computer and a classical computer using terms such as: (a) bit (b) qubit (c) electrons / photons (d) binary (e) logic gates

State the advantages and disadvantages of using quantum computers instead of classical computers. Note: Candidates will not be required to explain quantum theory related to the function of a quantum computer
Understand the purpose of variables and constants and initialise them in Python
Identify and use the basic data types: (a) (int) – integer (b) (float) – real (c) (str) – string (d) (bool) – Boolean
Use casting to convert between the data types in 8.1.2
Identify and use inputs and outputs

Demonstrate and use the following programming constructs: (a) sequence (b) selection • if, elif and else statements • nested selection • match-case (c) iteration • for loop (count-controlled) • while loop (pre-condition) • while, break (post-condition loop) • nested iteration (loops) (d) Understand and use the concepts of totalling and counting

Demonstrate and use the concept of string handling, including: (a) len() – length (b) .find() – find the position of a substring (c) .count() – count substrings (d) .upper() – uppercase (e) .lower() – lowercase (f) .title() – title case (g) .replace() – replace (h) + – concatenation. Note: The first character of the string is position zero

Demonstrate and use arithmetic operators, limited to: (a) + (addition) (b) – (subtraction) (c) / (float division) (d) * (multiplication) (e) ** (raise to the power of) (f) % (modulus division) (g) // (floor division)
Demonstrate and use relational operators, limited to: (a) == equal to (b) != not equal to (c) < – less than (d) <= less than or equal to (e) > – greater than (f) >= greater than or equal to
Demonstrate and use logical operators, limited to: (a) and (b) or (c) not
Describe abstraction as the process of creating a simplified model that represents the essential features of a problem
Explain the purpose of abstraction for a given context
Demonstrate how to use abstraction
Describe decomposition as the process of breaking down problems into smaller, more manageable sub problems
Describe how a problem can be decomposed into its component parts, limited to: (a) inputs (b) processes (c) outputs (d) storage
Explain the purpose of decomposition for a given context
Demonstrate how to use decomposition
Design, complete and amend algorithms for a given context using: (a) a flowchart (b) Python code
Explain the purpose of a given algorithm and the purpose of the component parts, limited to: (a) inputs (b) outputs (c) processes (d) storage
Complete a trace table for a given algorithm including inputs, outputs and variables for a given set of data
Identify and correct errors in a given algorithm
Amend an algorithm
Show how searching algorithms are performed on a given set of data, limited to: (a) linear search (b) binary search
Show how sorting algorithms are performed on a given set of data, limited to: (a) bubble sort (b) insertion sort (c) merge sort
Construct the algorithms using a flowchart or Python for a: (a) linear search (b) bubble sort
Describe the steps involved in a: (a) linear search (b) binary search (c) bubble sort (d) merge sort

Compare and contrast the features and efficiency of algorithms, limited to: (a) linear search (b) binary search (c) bubble sort (d) merge sort. Note: Candidates will not be expected to use Big-O notation when comparing algorithms. Note: Flowcharts may contain multiple statements in one box. Note: A decision box may combine a process and a decision

subtopics.title: Local and global variables and constants

outcomes.text: Demonstrate and use local and global variables
Demonstrate and use local and global constants
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of local and global: (a) variables (b) constants
Identify procedures and functions in a given context
Explain the purpose and concept of procedures and functions in a given context

Demonstrate and use functions, including: (a) sum() – totalling (b) .count() – counting (c) max() – maximum (d) min() – minimum (e) .mean() – mean average (f) round() – rounds a number (g) random.randrange() – random number generation (h) random.randint() – random number generation
Demonstrate and use procedures and call functions with or without parameters
Explain the purpose of a list including its features

Define, initialise and use one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) lists, including: (a) a variable for the index (b) writing into, and reading from a list including the use of iteration (c) iterating through each element in a list. Note: The first index is zero
Use Python’s built-in functions and operators for working with lists, including: (a) sum() (b) max() (c) min() (d) len() (e) .append() (f) .insert() (g) .pop() (h) .sort() (i) in, not in (membership)
Write algorithms for a: (a) linear search (b) bubble sort
Explain the purpose of storing data in a file to be used by a program

Demonstrate and use: (a) open() – open a file (b) .close() – close the file (c) with open() (d) "r" – open in read mode (e) "w" – open in write mode (f) "a" – open in append mode (g) .read(), .readline(), .readlines() – read the file (h) .write() – write to file
Describe the purpose of validation checks, limited to a: (a) range check (b) length check (c) type check (d) presence check (e) format check (f) check digit
Write Python code to validate input data for a given scenario, (inclusive and exclusive)
Explain the purpose of verification, including the function of visual and double entry checks
Write Python code to do a double entry check
Suggest and apply suitable normal, boundary and erroneous test data
Identify and debug errors in given Python code
Identify and explain the different types of programming errors, limited to: (a) syntax error (b) logic/logical errors (c) run-time errors
Demonstrate and use techniques that make a program easier to maintain, including: (a) meaningful identifiers (b) appropriate commenting (c) procedures and functions (d) relevant program layout
Define a single-table database from given data storage requirements, including: (a) fields (b) records (c) validations
Define a two-table relational database from given data storage requirements, including: (a) fields (b) records (c) validations
Identify data types, limited to: (a) text (b) character (c) Boolean (d) integer (e) decimal (f) date (g) time (h) currency
Explain the purpose of a primary key
Identify a suitable primary key for a given table
Explain the purpose of a foreign key to establish a link and join two tables
Identify a suitable foreign key for a given database
Demonstrate how two tables can be joined in a database
Write structured query language (SQL) statements using one or more conditions to retrieve data from a one and two table database
Correct SQL statements

Explain and demonstrate the result for a given SQL statement, limited to: (a) SELECT, FROM, WHERE (b) INSERT INTO (c) ORDER BY DESCENDING (d) ORDER BY ASCENDING (e) SUM (f) COUNT (g) AND (h) OR (i) INNER JOIN, ON
